correctness.rationale: The submitted universal claim is mathematically correct. When 0<=b<=sqrt(ac), N=max(sqrt(q_plus),sqrt(q_minus)) is a norm; r=b/sqrt(ac) in [0,1]. Any positive definite Q defines a Hilbert pullback. Averaging its two-sided comparison inequalities over all independent coordinate sign changes preserves the constants and cancels cross terms; hence it suffices to use Q=diag(u,v). Let A=a/u, C=c/v: on the positive quadrant the quotient is the Rayleigh quotient of [[A,r sqrt(AC)],[r sqrt(AC),C]], with maximum lambda_plus and minimum min(A,C). Writing z=max(A,C)/min(A,C)>=1 gives squared distortion D_r(z)=(z+1+sqrt((z-1)^2+4r^2 z))/2. If 2r-(z-1)>0, the difference of the relevant squared sides is exactly 4r(r+1)(z-1)>=0; otherwise the needed inequality is immediate. Thus D_r(z)>=1+r. At u=a, v=c the quotient is 1+2b|xy|/(ax^2+cy^2), bounded between 1 and 1+r, with equality at an axis and at sqrt(a)|x|=sqrt(c)|y|. All a,c>0, 0<=r<=1, including Hilbert r=0 and weighted l1 r=1, are covered. An independent SymPy calculation factored the squared-side difference and verified midpoint psi_r(1/2) and (2t-1)^2 remainder. These algebraic checks accompany but do not replace the universal proof.
